$comment: Provenance lock for the vendored hev-socks5-tunnel payloads under
What this replaces: the release pipeline asserted `test -s <file>`, which
proves a file is non-empty. The claim being made was 'the native tunnel
library in this APK is the one we reviewed'. Non-empty is not that claim,
and no step compared the bytes to anything.
HONEST LIMITATION, recorded rather than papered over: the upstream release
tag these three blobs were built from is NOT known. The repository carries
no build recipe, no upstream version string, and no note naming a tag, so
`upstream` below is null instead of a guessed version. What this lock CAN
do is detect substitution or drift of the committed blobs against every
consumer (CI, the APK gate, reviewers), which is the half of the problem
that is actually checkable today. Closing the other half means rebuilding
from a named tag in CI and replacing `source` with that recipe; until then
any statement that these blobs are provenance-complete would be false.
Alignment is recorded because Google enforces a 16 KB page size for apps
targeting API 35+ from 2027-02-01: min_p_align is the smallest p_align
among the ELF PT_LOAD program headers, measured from the shipped file by
scripts/verify-hev-lock.mjs, not copied from a build log.
